requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The code implements both obligations and the tests cover the main cases. A few test assertions are missing, listed under Gaps.

**Initial mandatory set**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`, marked `{impl}`) builds the contributed sources. These are the subject, the `{cite}`d requirements, the `{impl}`/`{test}` owning nodes, and the anchors.
- It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
- `definition_inputs` (`{impl}`) calls `terms::dependencies`. That function:
  - collects `{term}` references from the subject text;
  - collects them from each contributed input: Rust comments, Markdown or plain-text bodies, and the bodies of requirement blocks;
  - expands them to a fixed point with a `BTreeSet` and a `required.insert` guard. That gives no duplicates and no nontermination on cycles, and a missing target is an error.
- `source_input` (`{impl}`) turns each definition into an input whose `text` is the definition's `raw_lines` (`InputSelector::resolve`). That is the complete fenced declaration, including the `:phrase:` option.
- Duplicates are skipped with `mandatory.contains`.
- `initial_prompt` puts `mandatory_inputs()` into the first model request, and `assess` seeds `pending` with them. `pending` is recorded on the first response, before any submission is handled.

**Additional reads**
- `read` and `search` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` (both `{impl}`) call `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions` (`{impl}`) on what they deliver.
- It computes the same transitive set from the delivered inputs. It drops definitions already in the delivery or already recorded.
- The tool result carries the definitions, and `ToolDelivery.inputs` includes them.
- `assess` adds those inputs to `pending`. They are recorded at the top of the next loop iteration, before the submission branch runs.

**Marking**
- Every function that contributes to this requirement's behavior carries the `{impl}`. `terms::dependencies` is generic and is marked for `requirements.definitions.dependencies` and `selection`. `prepare` and `definition_inputs` reach it through the call above, and it has no `{impl}` for this requirement.
- I saw no behavior in the `{impl}` code that this requirement or another definition it implements fails to specify.

**Tests**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` builds two terms that reference each other (a cycle) and a subject that references only one. It asserts exactly two `definition` inputs, so transitivity, no duplicates and cycle termination are all checked.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks that a term referenced from a contributed Rust comment is included. It also checks that the term file's access policy is enforced.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` (`src/authoring/tools.rs`) reads an item whose comment references a term. It asserts that the definition is delivered, that two inputs are recorded, and that recording is deduplicated. It also exercises the `requirements` and `definition` read forms.

**Gaps (minor, not enough to fail)**
- No test asserts the definition's text contains the fence and the phrase line. That text comes from `raw_lines`, which the `definitions.inputs` tests cover elsewhere.
- No test covers a transitive term, or a term already recorded, arriving through an additional read. The `ripgrep` and line-range read paths are also untested for terms.
- Those paths all use the same `additional_definitions` helper that the item-read test exercises.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
